paragraphs: Rabbi Dostai, son of Rabbi Yannai. See Yalkut, II Kings 17: in the days of Shalmaneser, at the exile of the ten tribes, the king sent Rav Dostai, son of Rabbi Yannai, and Rabbi Savi; see there. So too in Keli Yakar, the aforementioned chapter. In Yelammedenu, section Vayeshev, and Pirkei de-Rabbi Eliezer chapter 38: Sennacherib sent Rabbi Dostai, son of Rabbi Yannai, and Rabbi Zekharyah—in Yelammedenu, Rabbi Savayya—to the Cutheans in Samaria to teach Torah. Do not think that he is Rabbi Dostai, son of Rabbi Yannai, Rabbi Meir’s student, mentioned immediately below, for there are a thousand years between them. This is very puzzling: ordination with the title Rabbi began with Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai’s students and thereafter, as the Arukh writes, entry Abaye. How, then, were Rabbi Dostai, Rabbi Zekharyah, and Rabbi Savi, who preceded Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai by a thousand years, called with the ordained title Rabbi?
